target_customer: Small businesses, designers and developers who need web forms without coding
problem: Building web forms and the database behind them required coding; Wufoo generated the form, database and scripts.

founders.name: Kevin Hale
founders.background_notes: Named as creator in YC description.

founders.name: Ryan Campbell
founders.background_notes: Named as creator in YC description.

technical_complexity.rationale: Auto-generating databases, form UIs and scripts with a polished builder was solid web engineering in 2006.

defensibility.rationale: Competitors launched the same year (JotForm, Form Assembly); embedded forms gave some switching cost, but features were copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google Forms arrived later and SurveyMonkey bought Wufoo in April 2011 as part of an acquisition spree.

market_need_then: Forms were the common entry point for web data; TechCrunch covered the July 2006 launch, and the idea came from Paul Graham during the YC interview per a Mixergy summary.

branding.name_origin: Reported in a company Q&A (seen via search, not opened) that Kevin liked Wu-Tang Clan and Foo Fighters

identity.mascot_or_character: No named mascot; current site uses dinosaur illustrations

branding.community_and_virality: Founders later became YC partners and talked about the design focus, but this record has no sourced evidence on fan accounts or merch.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct playful name and friendly voice, known in YC circles, though evidence is limited to the live site and one Q&A.

outcome_analysis: Wufoo launched in July 2006 after raising only about $118,000 and never raised again. The product reached enough paying users that SurveyMonkey bought it on 2011-04-25 for a reported $35M in cash and stock. A cheap, focused SaaS with strong design reached an acquisition without venture rounds, and it still runs under SurveyMonkey.
notes: Angel split conflicts: Mixergy says Graham and Buchheit put in $50,000, Crunchbase via HN says $18K YC plus $100K angels. Round recorded at TechCrunch's total of $118K. Price of $35M is reported, not company confirmed. Founder education and employers not found. The name origin is from a search snippet and is unverified. Rater confidence high on funding, competition and founders names but bios missing.
